title: Raw wolfCrypt errno from sess_init returned to userspace
description: In ioctl_init (crypto2dev_fd.c), when ops->sess_init() fails, the raw wolfCrypt error code (e.g., -173 = BAD_FUNC_ARG, -125 = MEMORY_E, -230 = FIPS_DEGRADED_E) is returned directly to userspace as the ioctl return value. wolfCrypt error codes are internal signed integers that userspace has no contract to interpret. Correct behavior: log the wolfCrypt error code, then translate to -EINVAL, -ENOMEM, -EACCES, etc. before returning. Additional risk: returning -EACCES only for FIPS_DEGRADED_E is important so userspace can distinguish a FIPS failure from a bad argument — returning -EINVAL for a FIPS degraded error actively misleads the caller.
close_reason: The global error convention at crypto2dev_provider.h:53-55 already requires all callbacks to return kernel errno. All wolfssl provider sess_init implementations call per-provider xlat_err() functions (wolfssl_cbc_xlat_err, wolfssl_rsa_xlat_err, wolfssl_ec_xlat_err, etc.) before returning — no raw wolfCrypt codes reach the framework. The one real defect was the agree() doc comment at line 247 which said 'wolfCrypt or kernel error code', contradicting the global contract. Fixed: changed to 'negative errno on failure'.
